critical_code_review_comments: App.js:1252-1271 downloadJson — <a> is now display:none but IS appended to document.body before .click(); URL.revokeObjectURL + a.remove() run after 6s. This is the correct fix; verified end-to-end via page.expect_download() in Chromium. Note: the setTimeout(6000) revocation is fine, but if the user closes the tab before it fires the objectURL will leak until GC; acceptable trade-off.
App.js:1274-1320 shareStudio + savePlaylistFile — both wrapped in try/catch and surface via setBanner; verified error path is not triggered for normal payloads and banner text is user-friendly.

playlistExport.js:132-157 — attempts array is well-ordered (stereo→mono, 44100→22050). eslint-disable no-await-in-loop is intentional and correct here (sequential retry). Friendly fallback message includes both duration and 'Save Playlist (.hl95playlist)' guidance. Solid.

server.py:669 SHOW_MAX_BYTES uses env SHOW_MAX_MB with default 200 and int() cast; server.py:814-817 raises 413 with the DYNAMIC cap in the message ('The cloud link limit is {cap} MB'). Good — cap is now configurable per env and the message auto-tracks it.

Nit: server.py:817 message says '{cap} MB' (int MB) but computes mb via '{mb:.0f}'. When SHOW_MAX_MB is fractional (e.g. '0.5') the int floor could report cap=0. Not a blocker; SHOW_MAX_MB is expected to be int-like.

rca of the issue: BUG 1 root cause was Firefox/Electron/webview requiring the anchor element to be in the DOM for a synthesized .click() to trigger the browser's download flow; the previous implementation created a detached <a> so the click was a silent no-op in those runtimes (Chrome tolerated it). Fix (App.js:1259-1266): create <a>, set style.display='none', appendChild to document.body, then click, and remove after 6s. Verified via page.expect_download(). BUG 2 root cause was OfflineAudioContext.startRendering() throwing 'failed to create AudioBuffer(2, N, 44100)' when a very long mix exceeded the browser's per-buffer allocation ceiling; fix (playlistExport.js) retries progressively at fewer channels / lower sample rates and, only if all four attempts fail, throws a user-friendly Error that the calling UI surfaces via 'export-error'. BUG 3 root cause was a hard-coded 50 MB cap in server.py; fix reads SHOW_MAX_MB from env (default 200) and reports the dynamic cap in the 413 detail. All three fixes verified in this iteration.
